did_you_know.text: Did you know? After Saul returned from fighting the Philistines, he was told that David was in the wilderness of En Gedi.
Did you know? Saul went to search for David with three thousand chosen men from all Israel, while David and his men were hiding in a cave.
Did you know? Saul entered the very cave where David and his men were hiding in order to relieve himself, unaware that David was behind him.
Did you know? David’s men saw this encounter as an opportunity given to him by the Lord, but David did not kill Saul; instead, he secretly cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.
Did you know? Immediately after cutting off the corner of Saul’s robe, David’s heart struck him, and he felt sorry for having even slightly damaged Saul’s clothing.
Did you know? David forbade his men from harming Saul because Saul was considered by him to be the Lord’s anointed, and therefore David had no right to raise his hand against him.
Did you know? David came out of the cave, called to Saul, and bowed before him, showing that despite their conflict, he still recognized Saul’s position as king.
Did you know? David proved his innocence with the corner of Saul’s robe: he showed that he could have killed Saul but chose not to.
Did you know? David left judgment and vengeance in the Lord’s hands, saying that he would not harm Saul, even though Saul was pursuing him to kill him.

Did you know? Saul admitted that David was more righteous than he was, recognized that David had repaid him with good instead of evil, and even said to David, “Now I know that you will surely be king.”
